title: Bring a dead consumer back, and only a dead one

blocks.text: Each of the billing service's queues has one consumer, kept running by a `Supervisor` that a scheduler calls every five seconds. A consumer can die on a message it can't handle, and the supervisor is there to bring it back. Two incidents in one week: after the first refund in an unsupported currency, the refunds queue stopped for good and the scheduler logged an exception from `check()` every five seconds. And on a quiet Sunday the invoices queue had nine consumers, each taking messages from the same queue.
Finish `check()` in `src/main/java/practice/Supervisor.java`. `newWorker()` builds a thread for the consumer with the right name.
When you're done, the first check starts the consumer, a consumer that died is working again after the next check, and a queue never has more than one consumer. About four lines.

cases.says: the first check starts the consumer on a thread with the supervisor's name
after the consumer died of an exception, the next check has it running again
a check while the consumer waits for work leaves it alone and starts no second consumer

origin.section: A Thread Runs Once: Run the Work Again on a New Thread

concepts: Whether a worker has ended is a question for isAlive(); a worker waiting for work is WAITING or TIMED_WAITING and alive.
start() is legal only on a NEW thread; to run the work again, a new Thread is created for the same Runnable.
